The Fleet

7 ships, 7 sailing, 23 entries kept. Each one carries one requirement from the profiles and each commandant keeps the same six-line stanza every morning of a 146-day crossing.

The chart is made months before departure and never revised. The window is set by orbital mechanics, the next one is 584 days later, and the transfer is already the minimum-energy path — so there is nothing to trade and all the thinking is spent up front. Readiness is the daily half, six lines against that chart, in a form that does not change, so that any two days can be laid beside each other.

Captain, bridge, operator — three hands before breakfast. A log signed by one person is a claim. A log countersigned the same morning by somebody who was also there is evidence, and that difference is what the settlement at the far end is actually paid against. The cargo is not what earns it. The record that the cargo was kept is.

The ships named for what they do, not for grandeur

Hestia

of the hearth, who does not leave, and does not arrive either

In the stories she is the one who stays — she has no wandering myth and she never leaves the hall. So she is the cycler: a permanent orbit that grazes both worlds and lands at neither, repeating on the 8:13 resonance that every calendar-keeper on the assembly page found independently.

6 entries · chart set eleven months before departure

 Iris

who fetches the water for oaths, and comes back carrying what light cannot

She is the other messenger, and the specific errand she is sent on is to bring up water from the Styx when an oath has to be sworn on it. So she carries the hydrogen — the one element Venus cannot make, the one cargo that is genuinely cargo, and the one thing a promise about this project actually rests on.

6 entries · chart set fourteen months before departure

 Atlas

who holds up the sky

He holds up the sky and does not put it down. The envelope is the same job: a membrane between people and an atmosphere that would kill them, held continuously, with no version where it is set aside for a moment.

2 entries · chart set sixteen months before departure

 Demeter

of the growing and the return

She is the seasons: the going and the coming back, the thing that grows because it is time. She carries the seed, the cultures and the soil starter.

2 entries · chart set twelve months before departure

 Prometheus

who carried it anyway

He brought fire to people who had been told they could not have it, and was bound to a rock for it, and his liver grew back every day so the price could be charged again every day. Daily regeneration and daily cost is the exact shape of a power system, and of a readiness log..

2 entries · chart set ten months before departure

 Hermes

who goes both ways

The only one who crosses between the worlds freely and comes back, and the one who carries messages rather than making them. He is the relay: 2.2 to 14.3 light-minutes each way, which is fast enough that nothing urgent ever needed a hold, and slow enough that no question and its answer are ever in the same conversation..

2 entries · chart set nine months before departure

 Charon

who is paid, and goes one way, and comes back anyway

The ferryman takes you across and does not bring you back. This one does, and that is the whole difference between a probe and a lift.

3 entries · chart set the morning of each descent, not a year ahead
